candidate.name: SELECTOR_GUARDED_OR_MERGE
candidate.definition: Introduce fresh selector s. Guard each clause C of A as (s OR C) and each clause D of B as (not s OR D).
candidate.exact_semantics: Setting s=0 activates A and disables B; setting s=1 activates B and disables A. Therefore SAT(M_s(A,B)) iff SAT(A) OR SAT(B).

shannon_reconstruction_theorem.statement: For A=F[v=0] and B=F[v=1], M_s(A,B) represents the same Boolean function as F after renaming v to s, modulo ordinary cofactor simplifications.
shannon_reconstruction_theorem.proof: For every assignment alpha to the remaining variables, M_s(0,alpha)=F(0,alpha) and M_s(1,alpha)=F(1,alpha). Hence the truth tables agree under v<->s.
shannon_reconstruction_theorem.effect: The selector merge does not eliminate the branch degree of freedom; it reifies it as a new variable.

rank_effect.reason: The child rank may have decreased after fixing v, but selector reconstruction introduces a fresh binary choice whose semantics is exactly the eliminated variable's Shannon choice. No universal strict single-state descent follows.
rank_effect.required_next_operation: To obtain real variable/rank elimination one must project the selector away: existentially quantify s from M_s(A,B), producing A OR B without retaining s.

projection_frontier.CNF_baseline: Davis-Putnam resolution is an exact CNF-level selector/variable elimination mechanism, but known resolution lower bounds block pure polynomially bounded resolution as a universal route.
projection_frontier.representation_baseline: Structured full-function compilation can support exact projection but has architecture-specific exponential state barriers already recorded in R44AC.
projection_frontier.open_scope: These facts do not rule out every SAT-sufficient compact projection invariant.

next_admissible_math.question: Is there one concrete SAT-sufficient selector-free projection invariant P(F,v), computable and representable in polynomial size, such that SAT(P(F,v)) iff SAT(F) and a fixed polynomial rank strictly decreases for every nonterminal 3CNF?
